'''''Paeonia broteri'''''  is a [[Perennial plant|perennial]], [[herbaceous]] species of [[peony]]. It is an [[Endemism|endemic]] species of the [[Iberian Peninsula]]. It bears rose-pink highly fragrant [[flower]]s about 12 cm wide and glossy green leaves. It reaches up to {{convert|40|cm}} in height.<ref>{{cite book|last= Page|first= Martin|authorlink= Martin Page (botanist)|title= The Gardener's Guide to Growing Peonies|publisher= [[David & Charles]]|year= 1997|isbn= 0-88192-408-3|url-access= registration|url= https://archive.org/details/gardenersguideto00page}}</ref>

== Description ==
''Paeonia broteri'' is a perennial, herbaceous plant of {{Convert abbreviated|30-80|cm}} in height. It is a diploid species with ten chromosomes (2n=10).<ref>{{cite journal|first1= A.|last1= Fernandes|first2= M.|last2= Queirós|year= 1971|title= Sur la caryologie de quelques plantes récoltées pendant la III Reunion de Botanique Péninsulaire|journal= Mem. Soc. Brot.|volume= 21|pages= 343–385}}</ref>

=== Roots, stems and leaves ===
It has carrot-shaped roots up to 3 cm thick, from which the plant regrows early in spring, when conditions are best for plant growth in its home range. It also has thin lateral roots. Its stems are often tinged purple. Its leaves consist of three sets of mostly three leaflets, which may be deeply incised themselves, resulting in ten to thirty oval or longish oval segments (1½-5 or rarely up to 6½ cm wide), with a wedge-shaped foot, a more or less pointy tip, shiny bright green upper surface, and a (nearly) hairless, distinctly blue-green underside.<ref name=PotW />

[[File:Peony seedhead. (Paeonia broteri) (40167068731).jpg|thumb|right|''Paeonia'' seeds]]

=== Flowers, fruits and seeds ===
The flowers are set individually at the top of the stems, are mostly subtended by one or two [[bract]]s looking like a leaf segment, and may be up to {{Convert abbreviated|15-16|cm}} in diameter. It has three, sometimes four, [[sepal]]s, green with a purple margin, of approximately 3 cm long and 2½ cm wide, with rounded tips. There are five or six magenta or pinkish magenta [[petal]]s, each 5–6 cm long and 3–4 cm wide. Numerous [[stamen]]s consist of cream-colored, yellowish or purple [[Stamen#Morphology and terminology|filaments]] topped with yellow [[Stamen#Morphology and terminology|anthers]]. There are mostly two or three (occasionally one or four, rarely five) [[Gynoecium#Carpels|carpels]] covered in 2 mm long rust-colored hairs, with at their tips very short red [[Stigma (botany)|stigmas]] of 2½ mm wide, their base encircled by a 2 mm high [[Glossary of plant morphology terms#Disk|disk]]. The fruit consists of two to three (seldom one or four) [[Follicle (fruit)|follicles]], each of which is up to 2½-4 cm high, and is covered in dense felty hairs which persist when fully grown.<ref name=PotW /><ref name=FP>{{cite web|website= Flora Protegida|title= Paeonia broteroi|url= http://www.floraprotegida.es/flora-vulnerable.php/Paeonia-broteroi-80/|accessdate= 2016-08-26}}</ref> In its home range, this species has flowers from late March to May,<ref>{{cite web|website= first-nature|title= Paeonia broteroi - (Paeoniaceae)|url= https://www.first-nature.com/flowers/paeonia-broteroi.php|accessdate= 2016-08-26}}</ref> but in The Netherlands flowering occurs in June and early July.<ref>{{cite web|website= PlantenTuin Esveld|title= Paeonia broteroi|url= http://www.esveld.nl/htmldia/p/pabrot.php|accessdate= 2016-08-26}}</ref> The seeds are about 7–8 mm in size, reddish at first but blackish when ripe.<ref name=Floramu>{{cite web|website= Floramu|title= Paeonia broteroi Boiss. & Reut.|url= http://www.floramu.com/verficha.php?ficha=60|accessdate= 2016-09-30}}</ref>

=== Differences with related species ===
''Paeonia broteri'' is closely related to ''[[Paeonia clusii]]'' and shares the same characters except for the different average numbers of leaflet segments: 11–32 in ''P. broteri'', 23–48 in ''P. clusii'' subsp. ''rhodia'' and 23–96 in ''P. clusii'' subsp. ''clusii''. ''P. broteri'' also looks like the [[Sympatry|sympatric]] ''[[Paeonia coriacea|P. coriacea]]'', but this species can be distinguished by its hairless carpels and wider leaflet segments (2–8 cm). ''[[Paeonia mascula|P. mascula]]'' may also be confused with ''P. broteri'', but this has only ten to eighteen (seldom up to twenty one) and larger (4½–18 × 3–9 cm) leaflet segments, while its carpels are mostly hairless and if present the hairs are about 2 mm long, whereas the densely hairy carpels of ''P. broteri'' carry hairs about 3 mm long. The distinctiveness of ''P. coriacea'' and ''P. mascula'' from ''P. broteri'' is confirmed by their [[tetraploidy]] (2n=20), while ''P. broteri'' is a diploid.<ref name=PotW>{{cite book|first= De-Yuan|last= Hong|year= 2010|title= Peonies of the World|pages= 159–164|publisher= Kew Publishing/Missouri Botanical Garden|location= London/St. Louis}}</ref>

== Etymology ==
The species was named in honor of the Portuguese botanist [[Félix Avelar Brotero]].

== Distribution and habitat ==
''Paeonia broteri'' naturally occurs mostly in the western part of the [[Iberian Peninsula]] (most of Portugal and western Spain) except the humid Northwest (north-western Portugal and [[Green Spain]]).<ref name="iberica">{{cite web |title=Paeonia broteri |url=http://www.floraiberica.es/floraiberica/texto/pdfs/03_056_01_Paeonia.pdf |publisher=[[Flora Iberica]] |access-date=22 January 2021}}</ref> Two specimens claimed to be from northern Morocco are probably from Spain.<ref name=PotW /> Despite its wide range, it is very dispersed through shrubs, oak or pine forests, in limestone soils from {{convert|300|to|1830|m|ft|abbr=on}} in altitude.<ref name="iberica" /><ref name="peonysociety">{{cite web |title=Paeonia broteri |url=https://www.peonysociety.eu/species/herbaceous/sect-paeonia/subsect-foliolatae/broteri/ |publisher=peonysociety.eu |access-date=22 January 2021}}</ref>

== Ecology ==
In the wild, ''P. broteri'' flowers between April and early June. Seeds become ripe in August or September. It grows in meadows, pastures and in the undergrowth of schrubs, pine and oak forests on well-matured soils on limestone, at an altitude between {{convert|300|and|1830|m|ft|abbr=on}}.<ref name="PotW" /> It is also common in rocky places and screes, particularly in humid spots. It grows together with ''[[Adonis vernalis]]'', ''[[Cytisus reverchonii]]'', ''[[Quercus rotundifolia]]'', ''[[Pinus nigra]]'', ''[[Pinus pinaster]]'', and ''[[Polygonatum odoratum]]''.<ref name=FP /> Plants that grow in different regions vary in the number of flowers per plant, in petal size, the number of stamens per flower, and the number of ovules in each carpel. These differences are related to the dominant pollinators, such as honey bees and bumble bees (''[[Bombus terrestris]]'') in the [[Sierra de Cazorla]] and smaller [[Halictidae|halictid bees]] in the [[Sierra de Jaén]].<ref>{{cite journal|first1= Alfonso M.|last= Sánchez-Lafuente|year= 2002|title= Floral variation in the generalist perennial herb Paeonia broteroi (Paeoniaceae): differences between regions with different pollinators and herbivores|journal= [[American Journal of Botany]]|volume= 89|issue= 8|pages= 1260–1269|doi=10.3732/ajb.89.8.1260|pmid= 21665727|doi-access= free}}</ref>
